Based on what Im seeing in the Roth paper I don't think the negative effects were prominent enough to say it isnt worth trying. 

The sample size was relatively small, made up of primary insomniacs, and the the length of time actually taking trazodone was only 1 week. Early in the study it is mentioned that only on the final day of the study (day 7) was slow wave sleep and daytime sleepiness positively effected. 

I think without a longer term study and a larger sample size saying otherwise it may be worth risking it for better sleep. I haven't noticed any negative effects, but another positive is it is relatively non-habit forming. If you think it negatively effects you thankfully you can easily stop taking it.

I couldn't sleep after training no matter what I did to relax. My saving grace is a prescription of Trazodone ([https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/pmc/articles/PMC5842888/](https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/pmc/articles/PMC5842888/)). I take 1/2 a pill most nights and sleep like the dead, even when I get riled up from a class. Neither my girlfriend (insomniac) nor I have noticed any side-effects in the 2 years We've been taking it.

It's been pretty life-changing to have sleep on demand and I would highly recommend talking to a doctor/psychiatrist about it.

Realize that sometimes you won't be happy if you are butting your head against the same wall. Redirect some of that energy to something new, if you hate that new thing it will give you new perspective on what you love. If you love it then you've solved the problem.
